title: Bouncing Ball
description: Interactive simulation demonstrating motion, velocity, and collision detection, with a Start/Pause control that emits a single xAPI `experienced` statement carrying the elapsed run time. Serves as the reference emitter for the Start/Pause dwell pattern in the xAPI Producer Contract v1.
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Physics
Motion
Velocity
Collision Detection
Kinematics
learningObjectives: Observe how speed affects the motion of a bouncing ball
Predict where the ball will travel after a collision with a boundary
Explain why a Start/Pause interval is the natural unit of engagement evidence for a simulation

keyQuestions: Pressing Start emits an interacted statement now — so why does the sim still need a separate experienced statement on Pause instead of computing duration from the two presses?
A student starts the simulation and closes the tab without pausing. What is emitted, and what is not?
Why do the Start and Pause buttons share one object_id instead of two?
Why does the speed slider get its own concept_id instead of reusing the sim's motion concept?
Why is the ball paused when the page loads instead of already moving?
Do the same actions in Full and then Compact mode. How many statements does each produce, and what does statements_represented in the compact summary tell you?
